text:
Dmitry Kuznetsov: FYI rolling NCCL 2.20.1 into the us-west3 A100 pool (canary 30%) and we started seeing intermittent collective stalls/timeouts during multi-GPU inference runs. Looks like allreduce/allgather hang with no obvious kernel OOM.

Carla M: @Dmitry any chance this is the canary only? how widespread so far? :eyes:

Dmitry Kuznetsov: Canary was 30% of nodes. Failures on ~6/20 canary machines so far, all A100 nodes connected over HDR InfiniBand. Single-GPU jobs fine. Multi-GPU (>4gpus) show ~99.9th percentile token stall for a few seconds, sometimes full job stall until timeout.

Ben H: What driver/kernel/firmware on those boxes? NCCL sometimes sensitive to mismatch.

Dmitry Kuznetsov:
- nvidia-driver: 535.104.05
- kernel: 6.1.76
- mlxfw: 18.36.1010 (reported from mlxup)
- container base: ubuntu 22.04, cuda 12.2
- NCCL: 2.20.1 (system install in runtime)

Alice W: Any commonalities in topology? same switch? same POD rack?

Dmitry Kuznetsov: All affected are on leaf-switch sw-usw3-12 and using same subnet for IPoIB. Non-affected canary nodes are on sw-usw3-07.

Carla M: Can you paste the failing log snippet? even short.

Dmitry Kuznetsov: pasted below (excerpt):
```
NCCL INFO Call: allreduce(), comm id=0x7f5c1b, op=SUM, dtype=FP32
NCCL WARN NET/IB: mlx5: send QP timeout, retry 12, peer 10.0.12.45
NCCL WARN NET: Socket/IB timeout detected, progress stalled
NCCL FATAL Unexpected error, aborting collectives
```

Ben H: That looks like IB QP timeouts and retries getting to maximum. Could be firmware + driver combo, or RDMA congestion. Did we see any switch logs or port flaps?

Dmitry Kuznetsov: No port flaps in host logs. Switch counters show elevated retransmits on sw-usw3-12 for the ports attaching affected nodes.

ops-runbook-bot: Ran quick diagnostics on affected nodes: pcie errors=0, link=up(hdr), mlx5 health=PASS, netdev drops=small(0.3%), tcp_retransmits=high(>200/min)

Carla M: OK. Two parallel hypotheses: 1) NCCL 2.20 changed some retry/backoff behavior exposing marginal RDMA conditions; 2) firmware/driver/IB firmware mismatch surfaced by new NCCL.

Alice W: Can we try the cheap mitigations first: set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 to force socket transport (slower but isolates RDMA) or set NCCL_NET_GDR_LEVEL/IB to tuning envs?

Dmitry Kuznetsov: Quick test: on one affected node set env and re-run small multi-GPU job: `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 python run_infer.py --gpus 8` -> no stalls in 30m smoke test.

Ben H: So disabling IB avoids stalls. That points to RDMA path. Not ideal for performance though. We need root cause.

Carla M: Freeze the rest of the 2.20 rollout. Revert canary to previous NCCL or pin to 2.19.x for now.

Dmitry Kuznetsov: Agreed. Rolling back the canary group now.

infra-bot: Action logged: rollback NCCL 2.20.1 canary in us-west3 A100 pool. Ticket: INF-4921

Ben H: Next steps: collect IB counters (rx_err, rx_drop, retransmits), mlx log, and enable NCCL debug logs `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` / `NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS=NET` for a failing job. Also capture `ibv_devinfo -v` and `ethtool -S` on affected and unaffected nodes for diff.

Dmitry Kuznetsov: Will gather and upload to INF-4921. Also will try two controlled experiments:
- repro with NCCL 2.19.6 on same kernel/driver -> expected no issue
- repro with same NCCL 2.20.1 but upgraded mlx fw to 18.36.1020 (if available) on one node

Alice W: If firmware fixes are needed we should coordinate with networking team and schedule low-traffic window. Could be need for mlx driver bump too.

Carla M: Also add a perf comparison: token/sec baseline on 2.19 vs 2.20 w/ IB disabled and enabled. We need to quantify customer impact before forcing downgrade across fleet.

Dmitry Kuznetsov: Noted. Initial numbers: 2.19.6 (IB enabled) = 1.0x baseline. 2.20.1 (IB disabled) = 0.55x. So big perf hit if we force socket fallback.

Ben H: We should escalate to NVIDIA/NCCL channel with logs and `NCCL_TESTS` reproducer. Also include switch retransmit counters and firmware details. I can open priority support if needed.

Carla M: Good. For immediate mitigation: rollback canary (done), add a preflight check to the rollout pipeline that runs an RDMA micro-benchmark between random pairs on the candidate leaf switch, and tag affected racks as blocked until fw/driver validated.

Dmitry Kuznetsov: Filing follow-up: INF-4921 (rollback + data), INF-4922 (canary preflight check), INF-4923 (firmware/driver validation and schedule).

ops-runbook-bot: Suggested temporary rule: auto-disable NCCL RDMA transport on nodes with retransmit_rate > 0.2% until fw/drivers are validated. (requires ops approval)

Alice W: Ops, please weigh in on whether auto-disable rule is acceptable. We lose performance but avoid customer errors.

Ben H: Prefer targeted fix (fw) over blanket disable. Auto-disable could be used as emergency stop-gap but must have alerting and rollback.

Carla M: Agreed. I'll coordinate with networking and schedule a controlled fw upgrade on a small set of nodes tomorrow. Dmitry please paste the NCCL debug logs when you have them.

Dmitry Kuznetsov: Will post logs to INF-4921 and cc @Ben H. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
